papers.title: HyLnc: a hybrid deep learning and feature-based approach for long non-coding RNA prediction.
papers.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play important roles in gene regulation, development and disease, yet accurate identification of lncRNAs from transcriptomic data remains a major computational challenge. Existing methods often rely either on handcrafted sequence features or deep learning approaches, each with inherent limitations in capturing the full complexity of RNA sequences. In this study, we proposed HyLnc, a computational framework that integrates transformer-based contextual embeddings with biologically meaningful sequence features for improved lncRNA prediction. A custom BERT-based mode
papers.summary: HyLnc is a computational framework that combines transformer-based contextual embeddings (a custom BERT model) with handcrafted biological sequence features to predict long non-coding RNAs from transcriptomic data. The hybrid approach aims to overcome the limitations of methods that rely solely on either handcrafted features or deep learning, improving lncRNA identification accuracy.

papers.title: Pan-cancer screening and integrative multi-omics and deep learning reveal the prognostic significance of an IBD-CRC shared host-microbe signature in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The prognostic relevance of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-colorectal cancer (CRC) shared host-microbe signatures in non-intestinal epithelial malignancies remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic and biological significance of an IBD-CRC shared host-microbe interactome signature in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA).
papers.summary: This study investigates whether a host-microbe interaction signature previously linked to both inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and colorectal cancer (CRC) also has prognostic value in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA), a non-intestinal cancer. Using pan-cancer screening combined with multi-omics integration and deep learning, the authors identify and characterize this shared signature in BLCA, suggesting that IBD-CRC-associated host-microbe biology may extend to other epithelial malignancies.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) under both redocking and realistic cross-docking conditions on three Alzheimer's disease targets. The authors find that the determinants of success differ between the two classes of methods, with AI approaches excelling in some scenarios but physics-based methods remaining competitive under cross-docking. The work highlights that no single method dominates and that performance depends on the evaluation regime.

papers.title: From Enhanced Sampling to Human-Readable Representations of Protein Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Understanding protein conformational dynamics is essential for elucidating biological function but remains challenging due to the wide range of time scales and the complexity of collective motions. Enhanced sampling methods overcome time scale limitations of conventional molecular dynamics, yet their effectiveness depends on the choice of collective variables (CVs), which are often difficult to define and may lack physical interpretability. In particular, collective variables derived from machine learning or collective vibrational modes can efficiently capture slow dynamics but are not easily
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of interpreting collective variables (CVs) used in enhanced sampling simulations of protein dynamics. The authors propose a framework to convert machine-learning-derived or vibrational-mode CVs into human-readable representations, making it easier to understand the physical meaning of slow conformational motions. This bridges the gap between efficient enhanced sampling and mechanistic insight into protein function.

papers.title: Multimodal alignment improves generalizability of genomic biomarker prediction in computational pathology.
papers.abstract: Computational pathology models that use digitized histopathology whole-slide images have the potential to become a cost-effective and scalable alternative to molecular assays for the prediction of genomic biomarkers, a key task in precision oncology. However, as new genomic biomarkers are discovered or quantified, large, labeled datasets must be prospectively collected to train new models. To address this challenge, we developed multimodal alignment for biomarker learning and generalization (MARBLE), a multimodal contrastive pretraining strategy that integrates structured biomarker knowledge i
papers.summary: MARBLE is a multimodal contrastive pretraining strategy that aligns histopathology whole-slide images with structured genomic biomarker knowledge, enabling prediction of new biomarkers without collecting large labeled datasets. This approach improves the generalizability of computational pathology models for genomic biomarker prediction, offering a scalable alternative to molecular assays in precision oncology.

papers.title: Multi-Sequence Fusion MRI Deep Learning Models for Discrimination of Recurrent Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma and Osteoradionecrosis.
papers.abstract: To develop a multi-sequence fusion model based on MRI images to differentiate between recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma (rNPC) and osteoradionecrosis (ORN) in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) after radiotherapy, and to evaluate its diagnostic performance.
papers.journal: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery
papers.summary: This study develops a deep learning model that fuses multiple MRI sequences to distinguish recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma from osteoradionecrosis in patients who previously received radiotherapy for NPC. The model's diagnostic performance is evaluated, aiming to address a challenging clinical differentiation problem where the two conditions can appear similar on imaging.

papers.title: Enhancing detection of polygenic adaptation: a comparative study of machine learning and statistical approaches using simulated evolve-and-resequence data.
papers.abstract: Detecting signals of polygenic adaptation remains a significant challenge in population genomics, as traditional methods often struggle to identify the associated subtle, multi-locus allele-frequency shifts. Here, we introduced and tested several novel approaches combining machine learning techniques with traditional statistical tests to detect polygenic adaptation patterns in time-series of allele frequency changes from whole genome data. We implemented a Naive Bayesian Classifier (NBC) and One-Class Support Vector Machines (OCSVM), and compared their performance against the classical Fisher'
papers.summary: This study compares machine learning methods (Naive Bayesian Classifier and One-Class SVM) against classical statistical tests for detecting polygenic adaptation in simulated evolve-and-resequence data. The authors find that combining machine learning with traditional approaches can improve detection of subtle, multi-locus allele-frequency shifts that are otherwise hard to identify.

papers.title: A Dual-Mode In Situ EV-miRNA Profiling Platform for Machine-Learning-Assisted Gastric Cancer Liquid Biopsy.
papers.abstract: EV-miRNAs are promising gastric cancer (GC) biomarkers for early diagnosis, yet their clinical application is limited by major detection challenges arising from the low abundance and high sequence homology of EV-miRNAs. Herein, we developed a dual-mode platform for sensitive EV-miRNA in situ profiling based on liposome-encapsulated localized exponential catalytic hairpin assembly (L-LECHA). L-LECHA enables the localized exponential catalytic hairpin assembly system to be delivered into EVs and activates exponential signal amplification, resulting in sensitive and rapid detection of EV-miRNAs.
papers.summary: The authors developed a dual-mode platform called L-LECHA that delivers a localized exponential signal amplification system into extracellular vesicles to detect EV-miRNAs in situ with high sensitivity and specificity. This overcomes the low abundance and high sequence homology challenges of EV-miRNAs, and combined with machine learning, enables a liquid biopsy approach for gastric cancer diagnosis.

papers.title: Few-shot neuromorphic vision in a nonlinear photonic network laser.
papers.abstract: With the growing prevalence of artificial intelligence (AI), demand increases for hardware that mimics the brain's ability to extract structure from limited data. In the retina, ganglion cells detect features from sparse inputs via lateral inhibition, where neurons antagonistically suppress activity of neighboring cells. Biological neurons exhibit diverse heterogeneous nonlinear responses, linked to robust learning and strong performance in low-data regimes. Here, we introduce a retinally inspired photonic computing system where spatially competing lasing modes in a random network laser act as
papers.summary: This paper introduces a photonic computing system inspired by the retina, using spatially competing lasing modes in a random network laser to perform neuromorphic vision tasks. The system mimics lateral inhibition and heterogeneous nonlinear responses of biological neurons, enabling few-shot learning from limited data. It demonstrates that nonlinear photonic networks can achieve brain-like feature extraction with minimal training examples.

papers.title: The fitness landscape of a form II rubisco in a photosynthetic bacterium guides engineering of oxygen tolerance.
papers.abstract: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (rubisco) is an important but challenging protein engineering target. Fast and selective rubiscos could enhance photosynthesis in plants and accelerate biobased production processes. To facilitate engineering of rubisco, we applied an in vivo screen that couples rubisco activity to growth rate of the photoautotrophic cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803. We screened a barcoded mutagenesis library of the form II rubisco from Gallionella sp. containing 15,000 single-site and multi-site variants. Exchanges in loop 6 near the active site, at the
papers.summary: Researchers screened a barcoded library of 15,000 variants of a form II rubisco from Gallionella sp. in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis, using an in vivo growth-coupled assay to map the enzyme's fitness landscape. They identified mutations, particularly in loop 6 near the active site, that improve catalytic properties and guide engineering of rubisco variants with enhanced oxygen tolerance for photosynthesis and bioproduction.

papers.title: Squidly harnesses enzyme functional hierarchy and contrastive learning to efficiently predict catalytic residues from sequence.
papers.abstract: Enzymes present a sustainable alternative to traditional chemical industries, drug synthesis, and bioremediation applications. Because catalytic residues are the key amino acids that drive enzyme function, their accurate prediction facilitates enzyme function prediction. Sequence similarity-based approaches such as BLAST are fast but require previously annotated homologues. Machine-learning (ML) approaches aim to overcome this limitation; however, current gold-standard ML-based methods require high-quality 3D structures limiting their application to large datasets. To address these challenges,
papers.summary: Squidly is a new machine-learning method that predicts which amino acids in an enzyme are catalytic directly from sequence, without requiring 3D structures. It combines a hierarchical representation of enzyme function with contrastive learning to improve accuracy and efficiency, making it applicable to large sequence datasets where structural methods fail.

papers.title: LLM-guided prediction of riboswitch-ligand binding affinity under data-limited conditions.
papers.abstract: Riboswitches are RNA regulatory elements that sense small molecules and regulate gene expression through ligand-induced conformational changes in an aptamer domain. They enable synthetic biology applications such as biosensing and gene circuit design. Accurate prediction of riboswitch-ligand binding affinity, quantified by the dissociation constant (Kd), is essential for rational riboswitch engineering. We present a neuro-symbolic framework in which LLM-derived embeddings encode riboswitch sequences, secondary structures, and ligand representations into a unified representation that captures r
papers.summary: The authors present a neuro-symbolic framework that uses LLM-derived embeddings to encode riboswitch sequences, secondary structures, and ligand representations for predicting riboswitch-ligand binding affinity (Kd). The approach is designed to work under data-limited conditions, where conventional machine learning models struggle. This could support rational riboswitch engineering for synthetic biology applications like biosensing and gene circuits.

papers.title: Mapping the combinatorial coding between olfactory receptors and perception with deep learning.
papers.abstract: The sense of smell remains poorly understood compared with vision and audition. At its core is an information flow in which odorant molecules activate subsets of olfactory receptors (ORs) and combinations of receptor activations encode distinct percepts. However, predicting molecule-OR interactions, and linking them to perception, remains difficult. Here, we develop MolOR, an approach that maps odorants to their OR-activation profiles and then predicts their odor percepts. Using cross-attention between a graph neural network over molecules and protein-language-model embeddings of receptors, we
papers.summary: MolOR uses deep learning to predict how odorant molecules activate specific olfactory receptors and how those activation patterns produce distinct smells. It combines a graph neural network for molecules with protein language model embeddings for receptors via cross-attention, helping bridge the gap between chemical structure and odor perception.

papers.title: Long-read based detection of large copy number variants with potential functional significance using the ContextSV structural variant caller.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing enables improved detection of structural variants (SVs) in the human genome due to its substantially increased read lengths. However, currently widely used long-read SV callers primarily rely on alignment-based evidence, limiting their ability to detect large and complex SVs and potentially missing disease-relevant events. To address these limitations, we developed ContextSV, a framework that integrates alignment evidence with copy number predictions derived from sequencing coverage and single-nucleotide variant allele frequencies to improve SV detection, particularly for
papers.summary: The authors present ContextSV, a long-read structural variant caller that combines alignment-based evidence with copy number predictions from sequencing coverage and SNV allele frequencies to better detect large and complex copy number variants. This hybrid approach aims to capture disease-relevant SVs that alignment-only callers often miss.

papers.title: Topologically distinct intratumoral heterogeneity scores for predicting high-risk pathological grades in invasive lung adenocarcinoma: A multicenter study across four institutions.
papers.abstract: High-risk subtypes of invasive lung adenocarcinoma (IAC), particularly micropapillary- or solid-predominant patterns, are closely associated with poor prognosis. This multicenter retrospective study developed and validated a predictive model for the preoperative identification of these high-risk subtypes using topologically distinct intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) scores derived from CT images. The study included 1,051 patients with IAC. Two complementary ITH scores were developed: a two-dimensional ITH score, which integrated local radiomics features with global pixel distribution patterns o
papers.summary: This multicenter retrospective study of 1,051 patients with invasive lung adenocarcinoma developed two complementary intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) scores from preoperative CT images—a 2D score combining local radiomics features with global pixel distribution patterns, and a topologically distinct variant—to predict high-risk pathological subtypes (micropapillary- or solid-predominant) associated with poor prognosis. The approach aims to enable non-invasive preoperative risk stratification, potentially informing surgical and treatment decisions.

papers.title: Dissecting genetic architecture and improving machine learning‑based genomic prediction of flowering time in Osmanthus fragrans by integrating structural variants.
papers.abstract: Sweet osmanthus (Osmanthus fragrans), a traditional ornamental plant in China, exhibits substantial variation in autumn flowering time, which significantly affects landscape application and cultivation efficiency. Here, we performed a genome-wide association study on 127 resequenced accessions classified into early, intermediate, and late flowering types, using a set of 2,325,410 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and 246,824 structural variants (SVs). By integrating SNP/insertion and deletion (Indel) and SV data with weighted gene co-expression network analysis, machine learning, and geno
papers.summary: This study dissects the genetic architecture of flowering time in sweet osmanthus by combining genome-wide association analysis of SNPs and structural variants with co-expression network analysis and machine learning. Integrating structural variants improved the accuracy of genomic prediction models for flowering time, highlighting SVs as valuable markers beyond SNPs for breeding ornamental plants.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Integration Identifies a Five-Gene Metabolic Signature With Experimental Validation in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is hallmarked by profound metabolic reprogramming; however, its intricate crosstalk with the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and its clinical ramifications remain inadequately elucidated. This study aims to systematically decipher the metabolic-immune interplay in ccRCC through multi-omics integration, with the goal of identifying robust prognostic biomarkers and actionable therapeutic vulnerabilities.
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple omics datasets to characterize the metabolic-immune crosstalk in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and derives a five-gene metabolic signature. The signature is experimentally validated and linked to prognosis, offering potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for this metabolically reprogrammed tumor.

papers.title: Machine learning approaches for cancer prognosis and diagnosis via non-coding RNA: a comprehensive review.
papers.abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), once considered genomic dark matter, are now established as key regulators of gene expression with widespread roles in cellular homeostasis and disease. In cancer, ncRNA expression is frequently and systematically dysregulated, and many of these molecules circulate in stable, protected form within biofluids, offering a compelling basis for non-invasive or minimally invasive diagnostic strategies. However, their clinical translation remains substantially hindered to date due to biological complexity, technical noise, and high dimensionality inherent to ncRNA expression
papers.summary: This review surveys machine learning approaches that use non-coding RNA expression profiles for cancer diagnosis and prognosis. It highlights that ncRNAs are frequently dysregulated in cancer and circulate stably in biofluids, making them attractive non-invasive biomarkers, but notes that biological complexity, technical noise, and high dimensionality still impede clinical translation.

papers.title: LAMBDA: a prophage detection benchmark for genomic language models.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based genomic sequence models represent an emerging frontier in computational biology. Yet, their embeddings have not yet shown the same level of predictive power as natural and protein language models, highlighting a gap between current implementations and theoretical promise. Existing benchmarks for DNA language models primarily focus on classifying regulatory elements in eukaryotic genomes, leaving open the fundamental question of whether these models learn sequence-level features across whole genomes. We introduce LAMBDA, a benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate genome langu
papers.summary: LAMBDA is a new benchmark for evaluating genomic language models on prophage detection, a task that requires learning sequence-level features across whole bacterial genomes. It addresses the gap left by existing benchmarks that focus mainly on eukaryotic regulatory elements, testing whether DNA language models can capture genome-wide signals.

papers.title: CAREPath: semantic context-aware reasoning paths with mechanism-augmented embeddings for drug repurposing.
papers.abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs that include drugs, genes, and diseases support drug repurposing by connecting drugs to diseases through gene-mediated multi-hop paths, thereby enabling mechanism-of-action reasoning. However, deeper traversal does not necessarily improve mechanistic reasoning: long paths grow combinatorially and frequently pass through hub genes, producing irrelevant gene regulatory signals, whereas overly constrained or sparse paths may miss broader biological context. We propose Context-Aware REasoning Path (CAREPath), a knowledge graph (KG)-large language model framework inspire
papers.summary: CAREPath is a knowledge graph–LLM framework for drug repurposing that generates semantic context-aware reasoning paths connecting drugs to diseases via genes, addressing the problem that longer paths often traverse hub genes and introduce irrelevant regulatory signals. It uses mechanism-augmented embeddings to balance path depth against biological relevance, aiming to improve mechanism-of-action reasoning over standard multi-hop traversal.

papers.title: DNAmBERT: a transformer-based model for non-invasive cancer diagnosis using DNA sequence and methylation data.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation alterations are early and stable hallmarks of cancer and represent promising biomarkers for non-invasive detection using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). However, current computational approaches often model DNA sequence and methylation features separately and struggle to capture complex read-level methylation architecture in heterogeneous, low-signal liquid biopsy data. Here, we present DNAmBERT, a Transformer-based deep learning framework designed to jointly model DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from cfDNA methylation sequencing data. DNA
papers.summary: DNAmBERT is a Transformer-based deep learning framework that jointly models DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from circulating cell-free DNA to enable non-invasive cancer diagnosis. Unlike prior methods that treat sequence and methylation features separately, DNAmBERT captures complex read-level methylation architecture in low-signal liquid biopsy data.

papers.title: AResKGLM: a graph-grounded language-model framework for interpretable multi-hop antimicrobial resistance reasoning.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens microbiology and microbiome bioinformatics because resistance phenotypes are shaped by interactions among genes, mobile genetic elements, and functional environments across microbial communities. Prioritizing resistance determinants requires models that reason across knowledge graphs (KGs) linking genes, proteins, pathways, drugs, and microbial phenotypes. Existing graph-based methods compress this evidence into scalar scores, whereas large language models can produce explanations not grounded in structured evidence. We developed AResKGLM (Antimicrobial
papers.summary: AResKGLM is a framework that combines knowledge graphs linking AMR-related genes, proteins, pathways, drugs, and microbial phenotypes with large language models to enable interpretable multi-hop reasoning about antimicrobial resistance. It aims to overcome the limitations of graph methods that collapse evidence into scalar scores and LLMs that generate explanations ungrounded in structured data. The approach supports prioritizing resistance determinants by reasoning across interconnected biological entities.

papers.title: From rules to foundation models: a comprehensive review of machine learning approaches for siRNA design.
papers.abstract: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) are a clinically validated therapeutic modality with eight FDA-approved drugs, yet designing effective siRNAs remains computationally challenging due to complex dependencies on sequence composition, thermodynamic properties, target-site accessibility, and off-target interactions. Over two decades, computational approaches have evolved from empirical heuristics to deep learning systems integrating physical priors with learned representations. We review the complete landscape of machine learning methods for siRNA design, spanning classical scoring rules, pretraine
papers.summary: This review surveys two decades of computational methods for designing small interfering RNAs, tracing the evolution from simple empirical scoring rules to modern deep learning systems that combine physical priors with learned representations. It covers the full landscape of machine learning approaches, including pretrained and foundation models, for optimizing siRNA efficacy and minimizing off-target effects.

papers.title: Analysis of lipid-protein interactive oxidation and underlying pathways in aquatic products via multi-omics and machine learning: a case study of air-dried hairtail.
papers.abstract: The interactive oxidation mechanisms between lipids and proteins during aquatic product processing remain poorly understood, limiting quality control strategies. This investigation employed a comprehensive approach by integrating multi-omics data with seven machine learning models to elucidate the mechanisms of lipid and protein interactive oxidation in air-drying hairtail. The optimal XGBoost model achieved 0.98 AUC with 0.90 accuracy on test set. Machine learning combined with multi-omics has identified six oxidative biomarkers of lipid-protein interactions: receptor expression-enhancing pro
papers.summary: This study combined multi-omics data with seven machine learning models to investigate how lipids and proteins oxidize interactively during air-drying of hairtail fish. The XGBoost model performed best (0.98 AUC, 0.90 accuracy) and identified six oxidative biomarkers linked to lipid-protein interactions. The work offers a framework for quality control in aquatic product processing.

papers.title: Identifying unmet needs in food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome using search query analysis and a large language model.
papers.abstract: Food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome (FPIES) is a non-IgE-mediated food allergy with many unanswered clinical and research questions. Existing educational resources, patient-facing education materials, and guidelines may not fully reflect families' information needs. Digital data and artificial intelligence (AI) offer new ways to identify public concerns in rare diseases.
papers.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. Global
papers.summary: This study uses search query analysis combined with a large language model to identify unmet information needs in food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome (FPIES), a rare non-IgE-mediated food allergy. By mining digital search data, the authors reveal gaps between existing educational resources and what families actually want to know. The approach demonstrates how AI can surface public concerns in rare diseases where traditional resources may fall short.

papers.title: DyAb: sequence-based antibody design and property prediction in a low-data regime.
papers.abstract: Protein therapeutic design and property prediction are frequently hampered by data scarcity. Here we propose a model, DyAb, that addresses these issues by leveraging a pair-wise representation to predict differences in binding affinity, rather than absolute values. DyAb is built on top of a pre-trained protein language model and achieves a Spearman rank correlation of up to 0.85 on binding affinity prediction across monoclonal antibodies targeting three different antigens (EGFR, IL-6, and an internal target), given as few as 100 training data. We employ DyAb in two design contexts: as a rankin
papers.summary: DyAb is a model for antibody design and property prediction that works in low-data settings by predicting pairwise differences in binding affinity rather than absolute values. Built on a pre-trained protein language model, it achieves Spearman correlations up to 0.85 across three antigens using as few as 100 training examples, and is applied to ranking and design tasks.

papers.title: HelixCross - Design and development of an AI-powered cross-examination simulation for forensic expert testimony training.
papers.abstract: Forensic testimony is where science meets the courtroom, and it is one of the critical forensic skills taught largely by apprenticeship. An examiner who overstates a match, mishandles a probability, or cannot support a method under direct or cross-examination can weaken the evidence in precisely the cases that rely on it. Yet in most forensic laboratories, testimony preparation remains largely informal, mentor-dependent, and unscalable. Consequently, many practitioners first face rigorous cross-examination at trial. To address this gap, HelixCross, an alpha-stage, publicly accessible, prompt-e
papers.summary: HelixCross is an AI-powered simulation tool designed to help forensic examiners practice cross-examination for expert testimony. It addresses the gap in formal, scalable testimony training, which is currently informal and mentor-dependent, by providing a publicly accessible prompt-based platform.

papers.title: Prognostic significance of DNA damage response-related markers in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma using machine learning approaches.
papers.abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) lacks reliable prognostic biomarkers. Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) has been implicated in genomic instability across multiple cancers, but its prognostic significance in ESCC remains unexplored. This study aimed to evaluate HRD score as a prognostic biomarker and develop a machine learning-based predictive model for ESCC.
papers.summary: This study evaluates homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) scores as a prognostic biomarker in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), a cancer lacking reliable prognostic markers. The authors use machine learning to build a predictive model based on DNA damage response-related markers, aiming to improve risk stratification for ESCC patients.

papers.title: A CFH- and SPINT2-based prognostic signature for cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a highly malignant tumor with a poor prognosis, and reliable biomarkers for postoperative risk stratification remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a CFH- and SPINT2-based prognostic signature to support postoperative risk stratification and inform adjuvant therapy selection in CCA through integrative machine learning and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.summary: This study develops a prognostic signature for cholangiocarcinoma based on the expression of two genes, CFH and SPINT2, using machine learning combined with single-cell transcriptomics. The signature is intended to help stratify postoperative risk and guide decisions about adjuvant therapy in this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: A token-pruning framework enables efficient representation of the human genome for RNA modification analysis.
papers.abstract: Modelling long genomic sequences remains challenging due to extreme sequence length, high redundancy, and the need for biological interpretability. Although Transformer-based architectures have achieved strong performance across genomic tasks, their high computational cost and reliance on fixed tokenization strategies limit their scalability and ability to focus on biologically informative regions.
papers.summary: The authors present a token-pruning framework that reduces the computational burden of Transformer models on long genomic sequences by discarding uninformative tokens, enabling efficient representation of the human genome. They apply this framework to RNA modification analysis, showing that pruning improves scalability while maintaining biological interpretability.

papers.title: Rational and computation-assisted engineering of a compact and efficient CRISPR-Cas12f genome editor.
papers.abstract: The CRISPR-Cas12f system is an ultracompact genome-editing platform, yet only a few orthologs exhibit robust activity in mammalian cells. Here, we systematically screened 23 Cas12f orthologs and identified two active nucleases, PspCas12f1 and TcCas12f1, capable of genome editing in human cells. sgRNA scaffold optimization enhanced the basal activity of PspCas12f1. To further improve its performance, we combined structure-guided rational design with protein language model-assisted filtering. Candidate mutations predicted by SaProt were further screened based on structural proximity to the DNA-b
papers.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
papers.summary: The authors screened 23 Cas12f orthologs and identified two active nucleases, PspCas12f1 and TcCas12f1, that can edit genomes in human cells. By optimizing the sgRNA scaffold and combining structure-guided design with a protein language model (SaProt), they engineered a more compact and efficient Cas12f genome editor.

papers.title: A computational framework integrating a protein language model with alchemical simulation for gain-of-function enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Engineering enzymes with enhanced activity and stability is a central goal of biotechnology, yet the inherent trade-off between optimizing global protein fitness and specific substrate binding affinity poses a significant challenge. Here, we present ESM-FEP, a computational framework that synergistically integrates a fine-tuned protein language model with alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) to overcome this limitation. Our workflow employs a parameter-efficient fine-tuned ESM-2 model to perform high-throughput saturation mutagenesis, rapidly identifying mutations that preserve protein fi
papers.summary: The authors present ESM-FEP, a computational framework that combines a fine-tuned ESM-2 protein language model with alchemical free energy perturbation simulations to design gain-of-function enzymes. The language model rapidly screens saturation mutagenesis libraries for mutations that preserve global protein fitness, while FEP refines predictions of substrate binding affinity, addressing the trade-off between overall stability and specific activity. This hybrid approach aims to make enzyme engineering more efficient than either method alone.

papers.title: A programmed cell death learning signature predicts immunotherapy response and identifies AP1S1 as a regulator of immune exclusion in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of global cancer mortality, characterized by profound heterogeneity. While immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has transformed oncology, its efficacy in breast cancer is often hindered by "immune-cold" microenvironments and immune exclusion. Programmed cell death (PCD) is a critical regulator of tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). However, its role in the breast cancer immune microenvironment remains poorly understood.
papers.journal: Chinese journal of cancer research = Chung-kuo yen cheng yen chiu
papers.summary: This study develops a machine-learning signature based on programmed cell death (PCD) genes to predict immunotherapy response in breast cancer, where immune-cold microenvironments limit checkpoint blockade efficacy. The authors identify AP1S1 as a regulator of immune exclusion, suggesting a potential therapeutic target to improve immunotherapy outcomes.

papers.title: scProtoTransformer: Scalable reference mapping across molecules, cells, and donors.
papers.abstract: The rapid accumulation of single-cell data has made it possible to comprehensively characterize biological systems at molecular, cellular, and donor levels. However, scalable reference mapping across different resolutions remains a major challenge in current research. Here, we propose scProtoTransformer, a prototype-based Transformer architecture designed to achieve scalable reference mapping across molecular, cell, and donor levels. scProtoTransformer introduces a knowledge-guided prototype tokenizer that projects gene expression into biologically interpretable pathway prototypes, effectively
papers.summary: scProtoTransformer is a prototype-based Transformer architecture that maps single-cell data across molecular, cellular, and donor levels by projecting gene expression into biologically interpretable pathway prototypes. This enables scalable reference mapping at multiple resolutions, addressing a key challenge in single-cell data integration.

papers.title: Programmable protein degraders enable selective knockdown of pathogenic β-catenin subpopulations in vitro and in vivo.
papers.abstract: Aberrant activation of Wnt signaling results in unregulated accumulation of cytosolic β-catenin, which subsequently enters the nucleus and promotes transcription of genes that contribute to cellular proliferation and malignancy. Here, we sought to eliminate pathogenic β-catenin from the cytosol using designer ubiquibodies (uAbs), chimeric proteins composed of an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a target-binding domain that redirect intracellular proteins to the proteasome for degradation. To accelerate uAb development, we leveraged a protein language model-driven algorithm called SaLT&PepPr to computat
papers.summary: This study developed designer ubiquibodies (uAbs) that selectively degrade pathogenic β-catenin in the cytosol, thereby disrupting aberrant Wnt signaling that drives cancer. Using a protein language model-driven algorithm called SaLT&PepPr, the authors accelerated the design of these chimeric E3 ligase-targeting proteins and demonstrated selective knockdown of β-catenin subpopulations both in vitro and in vivo.

papers.title: Integrating AI and Molecular Modeling for Structural Prediction of a Closed-Pore State of the hERG Channel.
papers.abstract: The voltage-gated potassium channel hERG (Kv11.1) plays a central role in cardiac repolarisation by mediating the rapid delayed rectifier K+ current (IKr). Blockage of hERG by small molecules can lead to delayed repolarisation, QT interval prolongation, and potentially fatal arrhythmias, making the channel a critical focus in drug safety screening. Despite extensive pharmacological and electrophysiological characterization, a complete structural understanding of hERG gating remains limited by the absence of an experimentally determined closed-state structure. Here, we use AI-based structural m
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This study uses AI-based structure prediction combined with molecular modeling to generate a model of the closed-pore state of the hERG potassium channel, which has not been experimentally resolved. The model provides structural insights into hERG gating that could inform drug safety screening for compounds that block this channel and cause cardiac arrhythmias.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed CAAC, a framework that uses ESM2 protein language model embeddings combined with genomic-neighborhood features and confidence-tiered neighbor voting to fill in missing functional annotations in silage microbial metagenomes. Applied to 21 metagenomes from inoculated and uninoculated silages across three time points, it achieved an F1-macro of 84.64% in cross-validation and improved coverage of carbohydrate metabolism pathways. This addresses a common bottleneck in metagenomic interpretation where many genes lack functional labels.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven prediction and design of cell-penetrating peptides for advanced drug delivery system.
papers.abstract: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) are promising delivery vectors for transporting therapeutic agents across cellular membranes. However, their rational design remains challenging because the relationship between peptide sequence and translocation efficiency is highly complex and nonlinear.
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence approaches are being applied to predict and design cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) for drug delivery. It highlights that the complex, nonlinear relationship between peptide sequence and membrane translocation efficiency makes rational design difficult, motivating AI-driven methods. The paper surveys the current landscape of computational tools for CPP discovery and engineering.

papers.title: Advancing precision tacrolimus therapy: a systems genetics dissection in BXD platform.
papers.abstract: Tacrolimus is a core immunosuppressant in organ transplantation, but its narrow therapeutic window and significant pharmacokinetic variability hinder precision dosing. Although CYP3A5-guided strategies have established clinical relevance for tacrolimus initial dose adjustment, they do not fully account for the marked interindividual variability in tacrolimus exposure, highlighting the need for complementary models to decode more complex genetic regulation. This study aimed to identify candidate genetic modulators of tacrolimus metabolism and develop an integrated predictive framework for indiv
papers.summary: This study uses the BXD mouse genetic reference panel to dissect the complex genetic architecture underlying tacrolimus pharmacokinetic variability beyond the known CYP3A5 pathway. The authors identify candidate genetic modulators of tacrolimus metabolism and build an integrated predictive framework aimed at improving individualized dosing in transplantation.

papers.title: Olink proteomics identifies serum protein biomarkers and an age-stratified diagnostic model for diabetes in Chinese patients.
papers.abstract: Aging is a critical risk factor for the progression and complications of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, routine clinical indicators fail to accurately quantify biological senescence burden in T2DM patients. This study aimed to screen plasma protein signatures associated with metabolic senescence in T2DM using Olink targeted proteomics and to construct a novel biological aging evaluation model for diabetic populations.
papers.summary: This study used Olink targeted proteomics to profile serum proteins in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes, aiming to identify protein signatures linked to metabolic aging. The authors then built an age-stratified diagnostic model that incorporates biological senescence burden, which routine clinical indicators cannot capture. The work highlights specific serum protein biomarkers that may improve diagnosis and aging assessment in diabetic populations.

papers.title: Deep DNA and protein level feature integration for robust clinical variant interpretation using probabilistic gradient boosting.
papers.abstract: A major challenge in clinical genomics is to classify genetic variations correctly, since it directly affects disease diagnosis and personal care. The existing methods tend to be based on the combination of different factors, such as protein structure, population frequencies, phenotypic annotations, and sequence conservation. Nevertheless, these methods often cannot be used to achieve the necessary interpretability, quantify uncertainty, and address rare cases. This paper presents a probabilistic gradient boosting model on variant pathogenicity prediction. The suggested framework applies biolo
papers.summary: This paper presents a probabilistic gradient boosting model that integrates DNA- and protein-level features to improve clinical variant pathogenicity prediction. The framework aims to enhance interpretability and uncertainty quantification, addressing limitations of existing methods for rare variants. It is positioned as a tool for more robust clinical variant interpretation.

papers.title: Time Series Transformer for long-term CD4 trajectory prediction in HIV patients: a novel deep learning approach.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of CD4+ T-cell trajectories is essential for monitoring HIV treatment efficacy and guiding clinical decisions. Conventional statistical methods provide population-level insights but struggle to capture nonlinear, patient-specific temporal patterns in real-world data.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This paper introduces a Time Series Transformer model to predict long-term CD4+ T-cell trajectories in HIV patients, aiming to capture nonlinear, patient-specific temporal patterns that conventional statistical methods miss. The approach is positioned as a deep learning alternative for monitoring treatment efficacy and supporting clinical decisions.

papers.title: Environmental PFOA exposure and the risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: An integrated computational toxicology and multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a pervasive environmental pollutant, has been implicated in hepatic injury and metabolic dysfunction. However, its role as an environmental risk factor in the pathogenesis of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) remains incompletely understood, particularly from a systems biology perspective.
papers.summary: This study integrates computational toxicology with multi-omics data to investigate whether environmental exposure to PFOA contributes to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). The authors use systems biology approaches to link PFOA exposure to molecular pathways involved in hepatic injury and metabolic dysfunction. The findings aim to clarify PFOA's role as an environmental risk factor in MASLD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Development of a PCR-based technique for genotyping UGT1A1 gene and distribution of rs3064744 alleles in the Russian population.
papers.abstract: Accurate determination of tandem thymine-adenine (TA) repeat numbers in the UGT1A1 promoter region (rs3064744) is essential for diagnosing Gilbert's syndrome and personalizing therapy with toxic agents like irinotecan and atazanavir. However, traditional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays face severe limitations due to the AT-rich sequence and overlapping melting temperatures (Tm) of the highly homologous 7TA and 8TA alleles. In this context, melting curve analysis (MCA) employing fluorophore-quencher systems has emerged as a promising alternative. The purpose of this study was to develop
papers.summary: This study develops a PCR-based genotyping method using melting curve analysis with fluorophore-quencher probes to accurately distinguish TA repeat alleles (rs3064744) in the UGT1A1 promoter, overcoming the difficulty of resolving the highly homologous 7TA and 8TA variants. The authors then apply this assay to characterize the distribution of these alleles in the Russian population, which is relevant for diagnosing Gilbert's syndrome and personalizing irinotecan and atazanavir therapy.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven identification and mechanistic exploration of synergistic anti-aging compounds from Dengzhan Shengmai formulation.
papers.abstract: Aging is a complex biological process involving multiple dysregulated pathways, and synergistic compound combinations offer distinct therapeutic advantages through multi-target and multi-pathway interactions. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulations are inherently synergistic, yet systematically identifying their active anti-aging combinations remains a major challenge. Here, we developed DeepSMCA, a deep learning-based framework integrating molecular descriptors, ADMET parameters, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network embeddings learned via a variational graph auto-encoder (VGA
papers.summary: The authors developed DeepSMCA, a deep learning framework that combines molecular descriptors, ADMET properties, and protein-protein interaction network embeddings (via a variational graph auto-encoder) to identify synergistic anti-aging compound combinations from the traditional Chinese medicine formulation Dengzhan Shengmai. The work aims to systematically uncover multi-target active combinations that are difficult to find through conventional screening.

papers.title: Etiology-Specific Nomograms for Predicting First Variceal Bleeding in Decompensated HBV- and HCV-Related Cirrhosis.
papers.abstract: Patients with decompensated hepatitis B virus (HBV)- and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related cirrhosis are at high risk of first variceal bleeding, yet etiology-specific and stage-specific prediction models remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate nomogram models for predicting the risk of first variceal bleeding in this population.
papers.summary: This study developed and internally validated nomogram models to predict the risk of first variceal bleeding in patients with decompensated cirrhosis caused by either HBV or HCV. The models are etiology-specific and stage-specific, addressing a gap in existing prediction tools for this high-risk population.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific immune cell state—JAML+ lipid-associated macrophages—that shows high transcriptome-wide association activity. By combining single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niche mapping, and machine learning-based selection, the authors link genetic susceptibility loci to a pathogenic macrophage program in the diseased liver. The work provides a framework for identifying cell-type-specific disease mechanisms in PSC.

papers.title: Machine learning-based early identification of heart failure/congestion complicating acute coronary syndrome using body composition analysis: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a major complication of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and is associated with poor outcomes.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study uses machine learning applied to body composition analysis to identify heart failure or congestion early in patients with acute coronary syndrome. The approach aims to improve early detection of this serious complication, which is linked to poor outcomes.

papers.title: Preventing relapse in ulcerative colitis remission maintenance: machine learning prediction and reinforcement-learning herbal prescription optimization with external validation.
papers.abstract: Maintaining remission in ulcerative colitis (UC) with traditional Chinese herbal medicine is challenging because fixed-intensity prescriptions may not accommodate changes in inflammatory burden. This study aimed to predict 52-week relapse and develop a data-driven policy for sequential adjustment of herbal treatment intensity.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to predict 52-week relapse in ulcerative colitis patients maintaining remission, then applies reinforcement learning to optimize sequential adjustments of traditional Chinese herbal medicine treatment intensity. The approach is externally validated, suggesting a data-driven framework for personalized, dynamic dosing rather than fixed prescriptions.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven identification and experimental validation of key biomarkers in the bile acid metabolic pathway associated with ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: Bile acids are shown to participate in inflammatory responses. This study was designed to investigate the functions of bile acid metabolism-associated genes (BAMGs) in ulcerative colitis (UC), identify the potential biomarkers based on eleven machine learning algorithms.
papers.summary: This study applies eleven machine learning algorithms to identify bile acid metabolism-associated genes as potential biomarkers for ulcerative colitis, then validates the top candidates experimentally. The work highlights specific bile acid pathway genes as candidate diagnostic or mechanistic markers in UC.

papers.title: Immune-Like Malignant Epithelial Programs Shape Tumor-Immune Interactions and Inform Prognostic Stratification in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is characterized by marked cellular heterogeneity, yet how malignant epithelial states contribute to immune regulation and clinical outcomes remains incompletely defined. We integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data to map the cellular landscape of LUAD and identify malignant epithelial cells based on inferred copy-number alterations. Epithelial states were further examined through trajectory inference, transcription factor analysis, and cell-cell communication profiling. Single-cell-derived genes were subsequently integrated with TCGA and independent GEO cohorts to
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-sequencing data to map the cellular landscape of lung adenocarcinoma, identifying malignant epithelial cells via inferred copy-number alterations and characterizing their states through trajectory inference, transcription factor analysis, and cell-cell communication profiling. The authors identify immune-like malignant epithelial programs that shape tumor-immune interactions and use single-cell-derived gene signatures to stratify patient prognosis in TCGA and GEO cohorts.

papers.title: Skill-File-Guided Virtual Screening: A Single-Target Formyl Peptide Receptor 2 Case Study of Large-Language-Model-Coordinated Physics and Diffusion Docking.
papers.abstract: Background: Virtual screening outcomes depend on protocol choices normally made implicitly by experts. I tested whether encoding that expertise as a "skill file" (a Markdown reference read by a large-language-model coding agent) changes virtual screening outcomes versus naive agent defaults, in a single-target case study on formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2; Protein Data Bank 7T6S, 3.0 Å cryo-electron microscopy). Methods: A Claude Code agent curated 1,000 pChEMBL ≥5 FPR2 actives and 9,829 property-matched decoys, prepared ligand libraries under naive and skill-guided protocols, and screened the
papers.summary: This case study tests whether encoding expert virtual-screening protocol choices into a Markdown 'skill file' that a large-language-model coding agent reads improves screening outcomes compared to naive agent defaults, using formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2) as a single-target test case. The agent curated 1,000 FPR2 actives and 9,829 property-matched decoys and prepared ligand libraries under both naive and skill-guided protocols for docking. The work explores LLM-coordinated integration of physics-based and diffusion docking in a structured, reproducible workflow.

papers.title: Integrating domain-specific convolutional features with Swin Transformers for transparent cervical cancer diagnostics.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer screening relies heavily on manual cytopathological evaluation, which is subjective and prone to inter-observer variability. While deep learning offers automated alternatives, existing models often struggle to capture both global cellular context and fine-grained biological nuances. To address this, we propose CAMF-Swin, a novel hybrid architecture for precise cervical cell classification.
papers.summary: The authors propose CAMF-Swin, a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines domain-specific convolutional features with Swin Transformers to classify cervical cells for cancer screening. The approach aims to capture both global cellular context and fine-grained biological detail, addressing limitations of existing automated cytopathology models. The work targets more transparent and accurate cervical cancer diagnostics.

papers.title: Interpretable prediction of nucleic acid-binding proteins using a protein language model.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) and RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) is critical for elucidating transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms. However, existing computational approaches often rely on inferred labels or domain-specific annotations, which limit the subsequent generalizability.
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable method for predicting DNA- and RNA-binding proteins using a protein language model, aiming to overcome the reliance of existing tools on inferred labels or domain-specific annotations. By leveraging language model representations, the approach seeks to improve generalizability across diverse proteins while maintaining interpretability.

papers.title: DeepVIC: modular prediction and classification of bacterial virulence factors using protein language model embeddings.
papers.abstract: Virulence factors (VFs) play critical roles in bacterial pathogenesis, and identifying these proteins and elucidating their mechanisms is essential for developing effective infection treatments. While protein language models (PLMs) have revolutionized the protein analysis, current in silico methods for classifying VFs primarily rely on fine-tuned PLMs ProtBert-BFD that perform identification and classification in a single step. This monolithic approach lacks flexibility and is vulnerable to error propagation, particularly from false negatives. Moreover, the direct use of PLM embeddings as feat
papers.summary: DeepVIC introduces a modular framework for predicting and classifying bacterial virulence factors by separating identification from classification, leveraging protein language model embeddings rather than a single monolithic fine-tuned model. This modular design reduces error propagation, particularly from false negatives, and improves flexibility compared to existing approaches like fine-tuned ProtBert-BFD.

papers.title: Computational mapping of resistance-relevant signals in proteins using deep and classical feature spaces.
papers.abstract: The functional diversity of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) proteins necessitates advanced computational frameworks capable of capturing complex macromolecular signatures beyond simple sequence homology. While traditional alignment-based tools identify known resistance determinants, they often overlook the underlying biochemical and structural properties that define novel or divergent resistant macromolecules.
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that combines deep learning and classical feature representations to detect antimicrobial resistance (AMR) signals in proteins, going beyond simple sequence homology. By capturing biochemical and structural properties, the approach aims to identify novel or divergent resistance determinants that alignment-based tools miss. The work highlights the value of richer feature spaces for functional annotation of AMR proteins.

papers.title: SA-FGPN: Stability-aware feature-gated progressive learning for pediatric brain tumor classification from high dimensional gene expression data.
papers.abstract: Accurate pediatric brain tumor classification from gene expression data remains challenging due to the extremely high-dimensional nature of transcriptomic datasets, where tens of thousands of features are available from only a limited number of samples. This imbalance increases the risk of overfitting, unstable feature selection, and unreliable performance estimation. Moreover, molecular heterogeneity among pediatric brain tumor subtypes makes robust prediction and biological interpretation difficult. This study aims to develop a stable and interpretable deep learning framework for pediatric b
papers.summary: The authors present SA-FGPN, a stability-aware feature-gated progressive learning framework for classifying pediatric brain tumor subtypes from high-dimensional gene expression data. The method addresses overfitting and unstable feature selection caused by the extreme imbalance between many features and few samples, aiming to improve both prediction robustness and biological interpretability.

papers.title: Cross-residual knowledge graph learning for robust multi-trait gene-trait prioritization in rice.
papers.abstract: Prioritizing genes associated with agronomic traits remains challenging because relevant evidence is distributed across heterogeneous biological resources and curated gene-trait associations are incomplete.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a cross-residual knowledge graph learning approach to prioritize genes linked to agronomic traits in rice, addressing the challenge of integrating heterogeneous biological data and incomplete gene-trait associations. The method aims to improve robustness in multi-trait gene prioritization, potentially aiding crop improvement efforts.

papers.title: Computational Characterization of Pathogenic LMNA Missense Variants: Structural Instability, Altered Binding, and Conformational Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Mutations in the LMNA gene underlie a broad spectrum of laminopathies, including muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, and premature aging syndromes; however, the molecular mechanisms by which missense variants disrupt Lamin A structural integrity remain incompletely characterized. Systematic computational approaches for prioritizing pathogenic variants and elucidating their structural consequences are critically needed.
papers.summary: This study uses computational structural analysis to characterize how pathogenic missense variants in the LMNA gene disrupt Lamin A, examining effects on protein stability, binding interactions, and conformational dynamics. The work aims to provide a systematic framework for prioritizing pathogenic LMNA variants and understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying laminopathies such as muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, and premature aging syndromes.
